note: Re-read Section 5.3 and all three tagged units. The server's structurally valid MRU Nak with only the Identifier changed leaves FSM, output and Magic unchanged, while its matching Nak sends a fresh request carrying MRU1400. The client wrong-Identifier Nak emits no replacement and cannot finish; the matching-Nak unit requires a fresh request Identifier, refuses the previous Ack and completes on the new Ack. The positive and negative assertions therefore distinguish the Identifier condition rather than blanket refusal. Explicit Max-Failure five preserves the old client inputs and assertions. Both receivers call ValidateLCPReply before adopting Nak options. Existing client revert records show the negotiator is exercised; their panic route is not claimed to specifically prove the Identifier guard.
